meaning: to agree with someone about an opinion or a decision
example: We do not always agree, but we see eye to eye on most things.
origin: Comes from the idea of two people looking at the same thing and having the same view of it

wrong_meanings.meaning: to look at someone very closely
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally. The idiom is about agreeing, not about looking
The idiom has nothing to do with eyesight or health
The idiom means the opposite: people who see eye to eye do not argue

explanation: 'See eye to eye' means that two people agree about something. It is used in relationships, at work and in discussions.
